overview: The Community Development Board approved site plans for two new Tufts University dormitories under Dover Amendment protections, released a bond for a completed residential development, and waived a full traffic study for a Medford Housing Authority project. The board also conducted an informal review of a proposed beer hall on Mystic Avenue and discussed establishing standing meeting dates.

items.title: Bond reduction request for 15 Ellis Avenue
items.summary: Approved the release of the remaining bond balance for two completed passive-house homes, following confirmation of city engineering sign-off.

items.title: Traffic study waiver request for 121 Riverside Avenue
items.summary: Approved a waiver allowing Medford Housing Authority to submit a traffic memo rather than a full traffic study for its planned 22-unit expansion and rehabilitation of the Saltonstall building.

items.title: Informal site plan review for 142 Mystic Avenue
items.summary: Reviewed a preliminary proposal by Great American Beer Hall to redevelop an industrial automotive parcel, with members offering feedback on landscaping buffers, exterior fenestration, and sustainability features ahead of formal site plan review.

items.title: Approval of board meeting minutes
items.summary: Approved meeting minutes from June 9, June 22, August 18, and September 8, 2022.

items.title: Site plan review for 2-4 Capen Street
items.summary: Approved a Dover Amendment site plan review to demolish a four-family dwelling and construct a four-unit, 29-bed Tufts University dormitory, subject to department recommendations and compliance with Tufts' commitments.

items.title: Site plan review for 50 Winthrop Street
items.summary: Approved a Dover Amendment site plan review to demolish an existing dwelling and construct a four-unit, 22-bed Tufts University dormitory, conditioned on off-site improvements, department reviews, and university commitments.

items.title: Future meeting schedule and Comprehensive Plan update
items.summary: Discussed moving to a regular standing meeting schedule on the first Thursday and third Wednesday of each month, and noted the upcoming close of public comments on the draft Comprehensive Plan.
